newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up a tad, eyes on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up a tad, eyes on Wall Street.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended flat to a shade firmer on Friday in featureless trade, with all eyes on Wall Street, dealers said.
"The market has been very quiet. The 100 points drop on Wall Street on Tuesday weighed on everyone's mind," said a dealer with a local institution.
He said there was renewed concern about a rate hike at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on February 4-5.
"The Dow might be affected if there is any rate hike. So today's trade is dominated by a very cautious, wait-and-see attitude," the dealer said.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended up 7.29 points at 2,224.08. Turnover was around 62.4 million shares, with gainers lagging losers by 164 to 170.
Uniphoenix Corp warrants led the actives with 9.8 million shares traders. Dealers said they were unaware of any corporate news that could have prompted the activity.
Multimedia company Aztech Systems saw 3.5 million shares traded after it became a trustee stock in which Singaporeans may invest their retirement funds. It ended up Singapore S$0.055 at S$0.485.
Creative Technology rose S$0.90 to S$15.50 while Total Access lost S$0.20 to S$6.70.
